chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever sells and buys, let him preserve five characteristics, or else he should neither buy nor sell: usury, swearing oaths, concealing defects, praising [the goods] when he sells, and condemning [the goods] when he buys.'

key_terms.الذَّمَّ: Condemnation or disparagement (of goods when buying)
key_terms.الرِّبَا: Usury or interest, often referring to the act of swearing oaths in trade in this context
key_terms.الْحَلْفَ: Swearing oaths (frequently used in trade to confirm the quality of goods)
key_terms.الْحَمْدَ: Praise (specifically excessive or misleading praise of goods when selling)

ai.seo_question: What are the five ethical characteristics a merchant must preserve according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s emphasis on commercial integrity by listing five key pitfalls: riba (often interpreted in this context as usury or excessive oaths), hiding defects, excessive praise during sales, and disparagement during purchases. These principles reflect the Shia scholarly focus on transparency and fairness, ensuring that transactions are conducted with honesty and mutual respect. The guidance underscores the spiritual and ethical dimensions of trade, aligning with broader Islamic teachings on justice and trustworthiness.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘

The one who sells and buys, so let him not practice five characteristics, or else he whould neither be buying nor selling – The interest (usury), and the oath, and concealment of the faults (in the goods), and the praise (of the goods) when he sells, and the condemnation (of the goods sold by others) when he buys’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy, who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘One who buys and sells must not engage in five things; otherwise, one must not engage in business of buying and selling: One must stay away from Riba’, swearing, hiding defects in the merchandise, admiring the merchandise when selling and belittling it when buying.’”
